title: The first wedding of the season (Tulsi Vivah)
caption:
The first wedding of the season is the tulsi’s. The rest of us are guests.

For the guests: the Emerald Deco Hoops, ₹1,249: green and clear cubic zirconia, not emerald, rhodium plated.

Dressing for a muhurat? Send the card and the outfit on WhatsApp, +91 95615 57935, and we’ll send back three matches with photographs.

Take 2 pieces for 10% off or 3 for 20% off. The bag applies BUY2 or BUY3 for you.

[ emerald deco hoops · rhodium plated · guests welcome ]
alt_text: A soft tulsi-sage tile. Dark green capitals at the top read: The first wedding of the season. Below, in italics: is the tulsi’s. the rest of us are guests. Lower down on the left, a flat paper-cut illustration of a tulsi sprig: seven pairs of oval green leaves with fine dark veins on long leaf-stalks, climbing a slim stem, their edges softly scalloped toward the tips, and three slender purple flower spikes with small flowers in spaced rings. To its right, at a distance, a pinked blush georgette swatch holds a pair of chunky silver-tone hoop earrings, the Emerald Deco Hoops, set all round the front with square green cubic zirconia between pairs of clear baguettes. A thin gold thread tied to the top of the right hoop arches out and down to an ivory tag with a sage window reading Shade N° 11, matched to the guests, green cubic zirconia, not emerald. Small type at the top reads The Match, N° 11, Tulsi Vivah, and at the bottom, The muhurats begin, guests welcome.

deviations: Sprig scale: the spec's flower spikes rise 110px from y190 to y80, straight through the eyebrow (Jost cap top y98, baseline y112, the line runs x72-566). Every sprig POSITION (stem, the seven nodes, the spike starts, spike length) is mapped by 0.9 about the stem's cut end (300,820): nodes at y730 / 658 / 590.5 / 527.5 / 469 / 415 / 365.5, stem top (309,253), spike tips y154 / 200 / 198; the highest ink (the central bud) is at y151.7, 18.7px inside the y>=133 limit, 32.7px under the eyebrow's line box (y90-119) and 40.7px under its baseline. Leaf lengths stay the spec's 130 tapering to 52 (sides differ by 3%), and every stroke width and dot size stays at spec. The stem base, the x90-500 column and the plant's bottom are unchanged.

Leaf drawing (the spec gives size, fill, midrib and veins, but no angles or petioles), per the art director's fix pass: pairs climb at 26 / 30 / 35 / 40 / 46 / 52 / 58 deg above level, each side 2-3 deg and 3% apart so the sprig is not a mirror image; bends -0.04 / -0.03 / -0.02 / -0.01 on the lower four pairs so their tips lift slightly, +0.02 / +0.05 / +0.07 on the top three so they cup inward (the earlier 4-28 deg lower pairs on a bare stem read as a neem or curry-leaf frond). Petioles 3px #3F5A4C at 30% of leaf length (tulsi's long leaf-stalks). Blades ovate, 0.49-0.53 of length wide, widest at 46%. Margins entire at the base and crenate from 35% to 92% of the blade: rounded bumps on a 10px pitch, 1.3px deep, each a true SVG quadratic curve (the first bump at 70%), replacing the 6px / 1.8px sawtooth that read as pinked fabric. The spec's 'finely serrated edges (6px teeth)' is therefore now a 10px crenation. Midrib 1.5px #E3EAE1 at 80% and three side veins per side, 1.1px #E3EAE1 at 32%, unchanged. 'Fills alternating' is applied as a checkerboard: the two leaves of a pair differ and each pair swaps.
Stem: 6.4px at the cut end tapering to 4.4px at the top (the spec's 6px, drawn as a living stem rather than a ruled line).

Leaf layering: inside the spec's whole-plant shadow (0 10px 16px rgba(31,46,37,.20)) each leaf carries a 2px soft shadow (#1F2E25 at 22%), so the paper-cut leaves separate where they overlap. No gradients added.

Flower spikes, per the fix pass: instead of the spec's even 'whorls every 12px', six spaced whorls per spike set from the tip down: 9px below the bud, then gaps of 10 / 11.75 / 13.5 / 15.25 / 17px toward the base, with the 4px #5E4A5E stalk showing between them and about 22px of bare stalk below the lowest whorl (tulsi manjari have spaced whorls; dense paired dots read as lavender). Each whorl is two #8E7A9A flowers either side of the stalk tapering d6 / d6 / d6 / d5.2 / d4.7 / d4.2, plus a third, smaller front flower (d3.6 #8E7A9A, set a hair lower) on the lowest three whorls so each reads as a ring; d4.6 bud at the tip. The two side spikes leave the stem in the axils of the top pair (spec y~296-300) and run as one curve through the spec's start points (280,240) and (346,236).

Claims (live listing text, 26 Oct): 'Square emerald green cubic zirconia alternating with pairs of clear baguettes', 'PVD rhodium coating', bright silver tone, about 22 mm; tags Cubic Zirconia, Rhodium Silver Tone Plated. So the tag's 'green cubic zirconia, not emerald' and the caption's 'green and clear cubic zirconia, not emerald, rhodium plated' are the listing's own facts. The product NAME says Emerald; the copy says what the stone is not. No 'gold' (this piece is silver tone), no 'diamond', no water, tarnish or hypoallergenic claim.

No em dashes, exclamation marks, emoji or urgency on the image or in the caption; no Tulsi Vivah date printed or captioned; no non-Latin script on this tile.
